messages:
Alex: FYI onboarding sample-app is flaking with 429s when it does paginate+batch-embed in a single flow. repro in 10s.
Meera: ugh, can you paste the short repro and logs?
Alex: steps: 1) start sampleapp quickstart 2) run /sync-articles which paginates article cursor 3) for each page we call embeddings.batch() in parallel with two gen calls. after ~3 pages we hit sustained 429s from API.
Alex: log snippet: ```
2026-10-12T14:12:03Z ERROR request failed status=429 route=/v1/embeddings model=text-embed-001 client_concurrency=8
2026-10-12T14:12:03Z WARN retrying after 200ms attempt=3
```
Sam: Is this the JS SDK or the go sampleapp?
Alex: JS (sdk-js@0.9.7) + sampleapp node quickstart. Also seen with the internal Go connector but behavior differs.
Lina: Could be our client-side throttle + paginator prefetch interacting. The JS SDK applies per-client token-bucket; prefetch spawns N inflight page requests which then each do a small batch embed -> bursts.
JD: I remember we changed adaptive-windowing to be per-client instead of per-route in #INF-3421. Might be related.
Meera: Interesting — so paginators are prefetching -> embeddings queued -> throttle allows short bursts -> API returns 429 -> SDK retries which increase concurrency -> backpressure spiral?
Alex: Exactly. Repro patch: reduce PREFETCH=1 and it mostly stops.
Sam: Quick workaround for customers: set env REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH_PAGES=1 or set client option {maxConcurrency: 2} until we fix.
Lina: Filed a minimal failing test for SDK parity across runtimes: https://git.redwood/infra/inf-3421 (private). Patch branch is `devex/fix-prefetch-throttle`.
Meera: What is the real root cause though? is it retry timing or bucket refill miscalc?
Lina: Initial analysis: token-bucket refill uses per-second refill but we allow bursts up to bucket size. Prefetch with parallel page requests drains full bucket quickly; then the retry/backoff strategy replays bursts at similar cadence leading to sustained 429s. In Go SDK we apply per-route buckets so embedding route was limited separately and avoided the spiral — parity gap.
JD: Proposed fix: (a) make prefetch default 1 on quickstart, (b) change JS SDK to use per-route token buckets, (c) tighten retry jitter and add exponential backoff cap.
Alex: I pushed a small sampleapp change (PR 4523) to set prefetch=1 and doc note for onboarding. Devs on quickstart should pull it.
Meera: Can we ship a hotfix to sdk-js? If we change to per-route buckets we need tests for multi-route sessions.
Sam: I'll take SDK side. Will add integration test that paginates and parallel-embeds and assert no >3 429s within 1m window.
Lina: I'll add a telemetry probe to Console to flag when a single session generates cross-route 429s so we can catch customers hitting this.
DeployBot: deployment queued for branch devex/fix-prefetch-throttle -> staging (run=ci-integration-27).
Alex: Thanks. For immediate support, I've updated the onboarding doc: "If you see 429s during quickstart, set REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH_PAGES=1 or set client maxConcurrency to 2."
JD: Ticket created: INF-3421 with priority P2 and owner=@Sam.
Meera: Great. Follow-up: once sdk-js fix lands we should revert quickstart to prefetch=2 and mark parity closed.
Sam: Will send a short PR and ping QA.
Alex: closing loop here, leaving the thread for anyone who wants to pick up telemetry + docs followup.
